name: Alhambra
description: The hilltop palace and fortress of the Nasrid sultans, Granada’s last Muslim rulers, with carved halls, courtyards, and fountains.

name: Huerta de San Vicente
description: The summer house of the family of the poet Federico García Lorca, now a museum set in a city park.

name: Sacromonte Caves Museum
description: A museum in cave houses on the Sacromonte hill, where Granada’s Roma community lived and shaped its flamenco tradition.

name: Federico García Lorca Park
description: A memorial park in Alfacar, outside Granada, near where the poet Federico García Lorca was killed in 1936.

name: Mirador de San Nicolás
description: A viewpoint terrace in the Albaicín, the old Moorish quarter, facing the Alhambra across the valley.

name: Plaza Larga
description: A small square in the Albaicín, the old Moorish quarter, next to a medieval city gate.

name: Royal Chapel of Granada
description: The burial chapel of Ferdinand and Isabella, the Catholic Monarchs who took Granada in 1492, beside the cathedral.
